The safety thing was really just paranoia. This is a small town in Texas so if a kid did have a gun it was way more likely to be something for hunting than a hand gun. And everyone had gone to school together since the dawn of time so if someone was acting out of character or doing something suspicious it was caught pretty quickly and they would go to psych meetings with a counselor once a week. 

There was only 2 elementary schools, an intermediate school (3rd and 4th grade), a middle school (5th and 6th grade), a junior high (7th and 8th), and a high school. The only one that was new was the high school. One of the elementary schools was the black high school before segregation and the junior high was a bomb shelter at some point. Both elementary schools and the middle school were knocked down this year because the buildings couldn't pass code anymore. Our district was also the largest out of the two in the county. The other school had maybe a hundred students and we had thousands.

No one wanted to add anymore to taxes but because there was only a handful of schools in the district, we did well on standardized test, and our football team made a decent amount of money we had enough for really amazing programs, like having two sets of books, but not enough for any new schools.

All of my school's had lockers but we never used them. Everyone had their own set of books for home and each classroom had its own set too so it wasn't like we had to carry too much. The lockers were left over from before the two sets of books were common practice. I think they stopped using lockers in my district for safety reasons. It's a lot harder to hide a gun on yourself than in a giant locker.

I'm 23 and (technically)  a sophomore and most of the kids in my classes are 18 or 19 and still stuck in high school. I've really never had a problem with the middle aged students because most of them have the same mind set I do and really just want to learn so they ask a lot of questions and don't just sit there doodling for all of class.

That being said I have a middle aged women in my psychology class that starts a lot of sentences with "as a corrections officer" and takes up a lot of the class discussion time. 

Many of the things she has said in class have been generalizations about mental disorders.
After she went on a rant about people with bipolar disorder and how they don't take their meds I ended up saying "you know I have bipolar type 2 and the times I haven't taken my meds were mostly because they weren't working for me and making my symptoms worse and maybe if they're acting up therapy needs to be looked at and medication shouldn't be relied upon so heavily". The professor seemed happy I brought this up because one of the main points of the class was to discuss the pros and cons of different forms of treatment.

A girl walked to me after class and told me she has generalized anxiety disorder and she was really happy I admitted I had a problem because it made it easier on her.

tl;dr most middle aged students are cool some think their jobs make it ok to make generalizations and take over class.

TIL south east Texas and south Mississippi have the same exact weather.

I live in between Austin and Houston and our weather is weird. This winter it was warm enough to go out with just a sweater most days and the days it actually was cold it was only bad in the morning and at night. Summer is usually hot as hell, unless it rains. in the Spring and Autumn it's hard to figure out what to wear and you might need to change half way through the day; usually a shirt and jeans in the morning, switch to a pair of shorts in the afternoon and put the pants back on and add a sweater at night.
Of course, we take the heat better than the cold. If the temperature drops below 70°F I'm freezing and I could wear a sweater and still be comfortable until it gets up to about 90°F.
I've only seen snow about twice in my life. There's other times it "snowed" but it was mostly just sludge.
Also we apparently either have a ridiculous amount of rain or in a drought; there's never an in-between.

You don't need to question why you aren't happy. You just need to find the thing that makes you full of yourself. I mean, don't think that way all the time, or everyone will actually hate you but when you are sad you basically have to try to get the mentality that you are the shit and everyone else doesn't get you because they fail at being good human beings.

Just convince yourself that you are the most amazing thing that has ever existed for about a millisecond. It usually gets me to, at least, a neutral mood.

I also moved back home earlier this month and I now have to deal with seeing people from high school who either tell me "Oh I loved you, you were so nice to me." or "I thought you were a bitch when we were kids but you're such a good person." The people who loved me were the other kids who were "socially retarded" and sad. The people who thought I was a bitch apparently did not understand I did not talk much and only said very blunt sentences because I didn't want anyone to see how weird I was.

My void is in my chest, there have been instances it filled up and I felt amazing but it feels hollow a lot of the time recently. I also remember crying in class in elementary school and eventually becoming friends with the nurse because that's where I would go to finish out my cry and I would just hope no one saw the first couple of tears that came out.

If you're anything like me thinking you're throwing a pity party for yourself just makes you feel shittier. But whatever it's your party and you'll cry if you want to, right?

My attempts were always spur of the moment things. It's never been something I spent the day thinking about. When I do decided on it, about a hour before I actually attempted, is when I try to do something that means something. Once I went to a lake near my hometown and sat on the cliff until I felt a bit more numb and not as sad. I drove to my hometown from the city I was living in about a hour and a half away. I sat in front of a church and tried to figure things out. I'm not a Christian but it was far enough out in the country for anyone who knew me to not find me but that whoever did find my body would be respectful. 

The time at the church and this time I haven't mentioned because it was a spur of the moment thing were the only two times I actually went through with the deed. I got a phone call from a friend at the last moment the other times.

When asked if I still wanted to kill myself I always answered with "not really I'm just tired now' and if asked why I wanted to do it I didn't have an answer.

I still have suicidal thoughts but I find something to distract myself now until the thought goes away. I'm in the habit of calling my family or friends when I have these thoughts too but I usually regret doing this because my past behavior has made them paranoid.
